Directions :Read the given passage and answer the questions that follow.

King Sagara, an ancestor of King Bhagiratha, once conducted an ashwamedha yagna to extend his dominion. When the horse went astray, the king sent his 60,000 sons to find the horse. Unfortunately, in the course of the quest, they ended up disrupting the intense meditation of sage Kapila, at whose abode they found the horse. Kapila burnt them all to ashes, sending them all to the netherworld - an act he instantly regretted when he realised what had happened. After breaking the news to King Sagara, he mentioned that the souls of King Sagara's sons could attain salvation only if the heavenly Ganga could be persuaded to flow over their ashes. It was Bhagiratha, whose austere penance and devotion pleased Lord Shiva so much so that he persuaded Ganga to descend to the earth. Ganga consented, but the problem arose that the earth would probably be unable to bear the intensity of Ganga's flow and even be shattered in the process. Thus, a solution was devised: Ganga would first land on Shiva's head and the locks of his hair would minimise the impact. Still, the force of Ganga's landing was such that it split into seven tributaries, three of which flowed east and three of them west. The seventh stream followed King Bhagiratha to the place where his ancestor's ashes lay. The river's waters instantly purified them. This is also the origin of the belief that the Ganga's waters can purify mortal souls of all their sins.

The above story is mainly about:
options_en: Lord Shiva holding the Ganga in his locks
the ashwamedha yagna by King Sagara
the coming of the river Ganga to the earth
the sage Kapila's anger for King Sagara's sons
questions.solution_en:
The story describes King Sagara's ashwamedha yagna, his sons being burnt by sage Kapila, Kapila's instruction that Ganga must flow over their ashes for salvation, Bhagiratha's penance to bring Ganga to earth, Shiva restraining Ganga's flow in his locks, and Ganga purifying the ashes.

Analysis:

Lord Shiva holding the Ganga in his locks: This is a significant event, but it's a means to manage Ganga's descent, not the central focus.

The ashwamedha yagna by King Sagara: The yagna initiates the story, but it's not the main theme, as the narrative progresses beyond it.

The coming of the river Ganga to the earth: The story revolves around Bhagiratha's efforts to bring Ganga to earth to purify his ancestors' ashes, culminating in her descent and purification, making this the central theme.

The sage Kapila's anger for King Sagara's sons: Kapila's anger and the burning of the sons are key events, but they set up the need for Ganga's descent, not the main focus.

Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.

Is the outcome of the action known to Mr. White?
options_en: Are the outcome of the action known to Mr. White?
Mr. White knows the outcome of the action?
It is asked if Mr. White knows the outcome of the action?
Does Mr. White know the outcome of the action?
questions.solution_en:
·The correct answer is (d) Does Mr. White know the outcome of the action?

·The subject of the Passive Voice is changed into the object of the Active Voice. Also, the object of the Passive Voice is changed into the subject of the Active Voice.

·The removal of the helping verb is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Passive to Active.

·Since the sentence is in interrogative form in passive voice, it should be an interrogative sentence in Active voice too. The answer to this question will be either "yes" or "no".

·These types of sentences usually begin with a helping verb like:

o Do

o Does

·Thus, the format of the sentence which begins with "Do" or "Does" in Active voice is: Do/ Does + Subject + V1 + Object?

·For example:

o Is therapy needed by him? (Passive)

o Does he need therapy? (Active)

·The options except (d) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Active Voice.

·Thus, the correct answer is:Does Mr. White know the outcome of the action?

questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

The architect will design a modern building for the downtown area.
options_en: A modern building for the downtown area will be designed by the architect.
A modern building for the downtown area has been designed by the architect.
A modern building for the downtown area was designed by the architect.
A modern building for the downtown area will have been designed by the architect.
questions.solution_en:
The subject of the Active Voice is changed into the object of the Passive voice. Also, the object of the Active Voice is changed into the subject of the Passive Voice.

The usage of a "to be" form of the verb [be] is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Active to Passive.

In Passive Voice, the preposition "by" is used before the object. However, it is optional in some cases.

The Active voice in this question is in Future Indefinite. Thus, the Passive voice will also be in the Future Indefinite.

The format of Active voice is: Subject + shall/will + V1 + Object.

Thus, in Passive voice, the format will be: Object of the active voice (Subjective case) + shall/will + be + V3 + by + Subject of the active voice (Objective case).

For example:

He will complete the assignment. (Active Voice)

The assignment will be completed by him. (Passive Voice)

The options except (a) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Passive Voice.

Therefore, the correct answer is: "A modern building for the downtown area will be designed by the architect."

Hence, option (a) is correct.

questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in reported speech.

Ryan said, "I did not use to have so many friends."
options_en: Ryan said that he had not used to have so many friends.
Ryan said that he did not use to have so many friends.
Ryan said that he used to have no friends.

questions.solution_en:
'Used to' express a situation or habit in the past. 'Used to' does not change in indirect speech.

For example:

She said, "I used to live in Oxford." (Direct Speech).

She said that she used to live in Oxford. (Indirect Speech)

The following things in the sentence should change when changed from Direct speech to Indirect Speech:

· Inverted commas ("...") are replaced with 'that'.

· The pronoun 'I' is changed into 'he'.

All the options except (b) are incorrect. Hence, option (b) is the correct answer.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Ryan said that he did not use to have so many friends.

questions.q_en:
Select the grammatically correct statement from among the given options.

A. He found a hourglass. It was a unique discovery.

B. He found an hourglass. It was an unique discovery.

C. He found a hourglass. It was an unique discovery.

D. He found an hourglass. It was a unique discovery.
questions.solution_en:
Option A: Incorrect

The word "hourglass" starts with a silent "h," making its sound begin with a vowel. Therefore, the indefinite article "a" is incorrect; it should be "an."

The phrase "a unique discovery" is correct because "unique" begins with a consonant sound, which pairs correctly with "a."

This is because "an" is used before vowel-sounding words, while "a" is used before consonant-sounding words.

Option B: Incorrect

The first sentence is correct as "hourglass" starts with a vowel sound, requiring "an." The article "an" in the second sentence is incorrect because "unique" starts with a consonant sound, so it should be preceded by "a."

Option C: Incorrect

As explained in Option A, "hourglass" requires "an," not "a." The second sentence is also incorrect, as "unique" shall be preceded by "a," not "an."

Option D: Correct

Correct use of the indefinite article "an" with "hourglass." Correct use of the indefinite article "a" with "unique."

Hence, option (c) is the answer.

Note: Definite and indefinite articles: In the English language, we have one definite article 'the'; it refers to or introduces a particular, specific noun. 'An' and 'a' are indefinite articles; they refer to, or introduce, an unspecified noun.

questions.q_en:
Parts of a sentence are given below. While the first and the last parts (A and F) are in the correct order, the parts in between are jumbled up. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent sentence.

A. Scientists

B. have developed

C. that

D. could revolutionize

E. a groundbreaking technology

F. renewable energy production.
questions.solution_en:
A. Scientists - This introduces the subject of the sentence, which refers to a group of scientists.

B. have developed - This shows the action taken by the scientists, indicating that they have created or invented something.

E. a groundbreaking technology - This describes what the scientists have developed, emphasizing that it is an innovative and revolutionary technology.

C. that - This introduces a relative clause, indicating that what follows will provide additional information about the technology.

D. could revolutionize - This specifies the potential impact of the technology, suggesting that it has the capacity to bring about a significant change or transformation.

F. renewable energy production. - This specifies the particular area or field to which the technology's potential impact is related, indicating that it is in the realm of renewable energy production.

Therefore, the correct order is ABECDF.

Hence, option (d) is the correct answer.

The rearranged sentence is: Scientists have developed a groundbreaking technology that could revolutionize renewable energy production.

Note:

Relative Clause: A relative clause is one that's connected to the main clause of the sentence by a word such as who, whom, which, that, or whose.

Example: He adopted a puppy that had brown eyes and black fur. The highlighted part is the relative clause.

questions.q_en:
Given below are six sentences, out of which sentences A and F are in the correct positions. Sentences B, C, D and E are in jumbled order. Select the option that gives the correct order.

A. Urban policy experts have long been arguing that the existing railway infrastructure in the state cannot meet the demands of the future.

B. The government claims the MONO project can take a significant load of traffic off.

C. This will make travel faster for commuters and reduce congestion on roads.

D. Most trains run at an average speed of 45 km/hr due to a lot of curves and bends on the existing stretch.

E. The state government began the process of land acquisition after the state's cabinet approval in June 2021.

F. Out of 1,383 hectares needed to be acquired, 1,198 hectares will be private land.
questions.solution_en:
The correct order is: ADBCEF.

The first sentence states that the current railway infrastructure cannot meet the demands of the future. D follows A as it talks about the reason for this. Therefore, AD is a pair. Sentence B follows and introduces us to the MONO project. It states that the project can take a significant load of traffic off. C follows B as it talks about the advantages of the project. The last sentence talks about land acquisition. Sentence E also talks about land acquisition. So, E precedes F.

Hence, option (c) is the correct answer.

questions.q_en:
In the following question, a sentence has been given in Direct/Indirect speech. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Indirect/Direct speech.

Kavya shouted, “I cannot work here hence I am going home”.
options_en: Kavya shouted at them that she could not work there thence she was going home.
Kavya shouted them that that she could not work there hence she is going home.
Kavya shouted to them that she is going home and that she cannot work here.
Kavya shouted to them that I was going home and thence I could not work here.
questions.solution_en:
"

The reporting verb is ‘shouted’ i.e. in past, therefore, the tense in reported speech must be changed according to past. So ‘cannot’ changes into ‘could not’ and ‘am going’ into ‘was going’. Changes to be made in personal pronouns i.e. ‘I’ changes into ‘she’.

"
